thread:
sam_support: Pasting a customer escalation — Acme reported a billing mismatch where dashboard token counts look ~1.9x of the invoice for streaming sessions last week. They believe reconnects/final chunks double-counted. They provided one example request id: req_0xabc123 and invoice INV-2026-03-09-ACME.
sam_support: Customer says flow is: client opens SSE -> partial deltas -> client disconnect (network) -> client reconnects to resume -> final chunk appears on _both_ connections in our logs. They attached a few log snippets.
sam_support: Quick excerpt from their client trace: 
```
[client] CONNECT stream_id=stream-77
[client] receive delta tokens=132
[network] TCP reset
[client] RECONNECT stream_id=stream-77 resume=true
[client] receive final tokens=48
```
sam_support: They claim dashboard shows ~312 tokens for that session but invoice shows ~150 tokens billed; in other cases the invoice is higher than dashboard. So both over- and under-counting reported across different customers.
ali_billing: @sam_support can you attach the invoice id and the canonical list of request ids? we need the raw metering events window to reconcile. Also need the customer's account id.
sam_support: Sent INV-2026-03-09-ACME and account acme-corp in a DM. Pasted the two request ids they gave: req_0xabc123, req_0xabc124. I also attached their sample SSE log to the ticket.
metering-bot: FYI automated alert: duplicate-final-token-events detected for stream-77 on 2026-03-09 02:12:34 UTC (trace req_0xabc123). Count anomaly score 0.78.
maria_eng_runtime: Thanks — I pulled the runtime trace for req_0xabc123. I can see two "final" frames emitted: one tied to the original connection, and one tied to the resumed connection. The sequence_ids are different but the stream_id matches.
maria_eng_runtime: Runtime excerpt: 
```
[runtime] conn=conn-A stream=stream-77 event=delta tokens=132 seq=15
[runtime] conn=conn-A stream=stream-77 event=final tokens=0 seq=16 (connection closed mid-event)
[runtime] conn=conn-B stream=stream-77 event=final tokens=48 seq=17 resume=true
```
maria_eng_runtime: The interesting bit is the mid-event close. conn-A logged a final with 0 tokens (we flush partial), then conn-B logs final with 48. Our metering pipeline currently aggregates token events at the connection level then sums per stream. If a stream is resumed on a new connection we end up counting both connection-level finals.
kevin_oncall: That matches a hypothesis I had during the 02:00 incident. We saw a reconnect storm and some meter writer jobs retried. Could be a race between the "write final" and the billing dedupe TTL.
ali_billing: Do we have a unique stream/session id we can use as a dedupe key? If so we can retroactively dedupe for invoices in the affected window.
maria_eng_runtime: stream-77 is a stable session id from the client — the issue is we stamp metering records with connection_id + sequence windows. We do set session_id but our metering writer shards only dedup within connection_id for 30s; if resume happens on a different connection it misses dedupe.
maria_eng_runtime: Proposed fix: extend dedupe window to include session_id across connections for streaming final events and mark final event as the authoritative end-of-stream. Also make final events idempotent by adding a final_event_id derived from session_id + final_seq.
ali_billing: For remediation: Can we produce a backfill that groups metering events by session_id and takes the max token count per session for the invoice period? we should also flag any invoices where aggregated credits/charges change >5% and notify finance + customer.
maria_eng_runtime: Yes — I can prototype a backfill SQL that collapses by session_id and uses greatest(token_sum, server_reported_total). But need to be careful: some sessions legitimately had multiple independent streams with same session_id pattern. I'll prepare filters: timeframe, account id, request ids.
kevin_oncall: Estimate of blast radius? How many customers hit this? quick grep shows ~142 session resume events across prod in that 3-hour window, ~38 distinct accounts. Potential invoice exposure ~ $2.3k (gross), probably fewer after dedupe.
sam_support: Customer has asked for a timeline; they'd like a credit if invoice ends up higher. They also want to know what prevented double-charging in other events where invoice lower than dashboard.
maria_eng_runtime: Lower invoice vs dashboard: separate issue — async metrics pipeline undercount due to missing completion ack from the metering writer during a transient outage; dashboard pulls near-real-time counters while invoice uses completed writes. We'll need two things: 1) fix the dedupe across resumes to prevent overcounting 2) reconcile missing writes leading to undercount and backfill those when possible.
ali_billing: Action items: (1) run dedupe backfill for INV-2026-03-09-ACME and any invoices for accounts in the 02:00-05:00 UTC window; (2) prepare credit memos for any customers where billing decreases; (3) hold credits until engineering confirms safe dedupe logic.
maria_eng_runtime: I'll implement the runtime dedupe patch and tests today. Patch plan: mark final events with final_event_id and ensure metering-writer dedupes by final_event_id across connection_id for 24h. I'll post PR when ready.
kevin_oncall: If we need emergency rollouts, ping me — but prefer a staged canary to avoid new regressions.
sam_support: I'll reply to the customer with: we're investigating, will run a focused reconciliation for their invoice, and will follow up with credits if needed. :eyes:
ali_billing: Please attach affected invoice ids to the billing ticket and CC finance. I'll start a draft credit memo workflow.
metering-bot: Backfill job queued: job_id=bf-1956789123-1 target_accounts=[acme-corp] window=2026-03-09T02:00:00Z/2026-03-09T05:00:00Z
sam_support: Thanks everyone. Keep this thread updated — customer asked for ETA within 48h.
maria_eng_runtime: PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/734 — includes unit tests for resume dedupe and a migration for final_event_id. Planning canary deploy to staging tonight.
kevin_oncall: Noted. I'll monitor the canary. Once engineering confirms backfill output, @ali_billing you can finalize credits.
ali_billing: Will do. Sam — let the customer know target ETA 48h and we'll update as we make progress. :thumbsup:
